messages:
Sam (support): Hey team, customer ACME corp started failing SSO since their IdP cert rotation yesterday. Getting `InvalidAssertion: Recipient mismatch` in our logs. They say they updated metadata. Ticket: https://support.redwood.example/tickets/RC-9421 :face_with_raised_eyebrow:
Maria (eng): Can you paste the raw SAMLResponse or relevant log lines? Is this during SP-initiated or IdP-initiated flow?
Sam (support): SP-initiated. Log excerpt: 
```
2026-03-10T14:02:11Z ERROR saml-handler - InvalidAssertion: Assertion Recipient does not match ACS URL (expected https://app.acme.example/saml/acs, got https://app.acme.example/saml/acs/)
stack: saml.VerifyError at saml.verify (/srv/saml/index.js:212:18)
```
Also noticed IdP metadata shows two AssertionConsumerService entries — one with trailing slash. Customer says they removed trailing slash but our calls still see it.
Jordan (sre): Could be a reverse proxy caching the old metadata or a CDN in front of the IdP. Also check clock skew and audience. But the trailing slash is telling. Did they rotate certs too?
Sam (support): Yes they rotated cert last night. They provided new metadata XML but when I fetch it from their metadata URL I see old cert and the ACS with trailing slash. I asked them to re-publish.
Maria (eng): Can you paste the metadata snippet? Also what's our code doing for Recipient comparison — strict equality or normalized? We normalize host but not path slash by default.
Sam (support): Snippet from the metadata we fetched: 
```
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.acme.example">
  <SPSSODescriptor>
    <AssertionConsumerService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST" Location="https://app.acme.example/saml/acs/" index="0"/>
    <AssertionConsumerService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST" Location="https://app.acme.example/saml/acs" index="1"/>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo><X509Data><X509Certificate>MIIC...OLDCERT...</X509Certificate></X509Data></KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
  </SPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```
Note the cert is old.
Elaine (prod): @Maria (eng) we recently tightened Recipient compare to avoid open redirect exploits. That will fail if IdP publishes alternate ACS URL with trailing slash. Two options: normalize on both sides or ask IdP to publish canonical ACS only. But the cert being old suggests they didn't actually update metadata endpoint.
Maria (eng): Right. Let's avoid making policy changes without owner approval. Quick repro: Sam, can you `curl -I` the metadata URL and show `Cache-Control` and `Age` headers? Also share the metadata URL.
Sam (support): Metadata URL: https://idp.acme.example/.well-known/saml/metadata.xml
Output:
```
HTTP/2 200
content-type: application/samlmetadata+xml
cache-control: public, max-age=86400
age: 43200
```
So there's a 24h TTL and the CDN still has old content. Customer claims they uploaded new metadata but their CDN origin didn't purge.
Jordan (sre): That explains it. Cert rotation alone isn't enough; metadata cache must be purged. Steps to repro locally: 1) fetch metadata before rotation 2) rotate IdP cert and update metadata at origin 3) don't purge CDN 4) our SP fetches metadata and still sees old cert -> signature validation fails OR Recipient mismatch if metadata entry order has alternate ACS.
Maria (eng): For short-term fix, we can tolerate trailing slash by normalizing ACS URLs during Recipient check: strip trailing slashes before comparing. But we need to log when normalization happened to audit security impact. I'll open a tiny patch and flag for review.
Elaine (prod): Also ask customer to purge CDN and confirm fingerprint. Commands for them: 
```
# verify published cert fingerprint
curl -s https://idp.acme.example/.well-known/saml/metadata.xml | xmllint --xpath '//KeyDescriptor//X509Certificate/text()' - | base64 --decode > idp.crt
openssl x509 -noout -in idp.crt -fingerprint -sha256
```
Send us SHA256 fingerprint to confirm.
Sam (support): I sent those commands and asked them to purge their CDN. They responded they accidentally uploaded metadata to a staging bucket and didn't invalidate the prod CDN. They're purging now.
deploy-bot: deployment started: saml-normalize-slashes v0.1 -> staging :rocket:
Maria (eng): Quick note for postmortem: add a monitoring alert if metadata fetch returns `Age` > 3600 (1h) after a cert rotation event logged from the IdP domain. Also add a small diagnostic endpoint `/_saml/metadata-source` that returns the metadata we fetched and its `Cache-Control` headers for troubleshooting.
Sam (support): Customer confirmed purge and after ~60s our logs show successful login. I told them to re-run the fingerprint check. Ticket RC-9421 updated. :tada:
Elaine (prod): Good to close once you get their confirmation that they rotated and purged. Create a short internal KB with the `curl` + `openssl` steps we used.
Sam (support): Will do. Thanks everyone. :heart:
